title: What is reward dripping, and why can't rewards be spawned like on an ICP neuron?
text:
What is reward dripping, and why can't rewards be spawned like on an ICP neuron?

If you have the "Automatically stake new maturity" setting enabled, rewards your neuron earns are immediately locked back into the neuron as soon as they are distributed. That means the rewards are automatically staked rather than remaining as separate maturity you could "spawn". This produces compounding rewards because your neuron's voting power is calculated from its stake plus its staked maturity.

title: How do I 'hotkey' my user ID so I can vote on Proposals? I get an error telling me to hotkey my ID but not how to do it.
text:
How do I 'hotkey' my user ID so I can vote on Proposals? I get an error telling me to hotkey my ID but not how to do it.

You must add your user-id as a hotkey of your CHAT neuron on the NNS (Network Nervous System). If you do not have a CHAT neuron, you will not be able to vote on proposals. For step-by-step instructions, see the OpenChat governance guide (e.g. https://oc.app/blog/governance).

title: Why is scrolling smooth on mobile and in desktop Gecko (Firefox) browsers but jerky in desktop Chromium-based browsers?
text:
Why is scrolling smooth on mobile and in desktop Gecko (Firefox) browsers but jerky in desktop Chromium-based browsers?

On phones the OS often handles scrolling on a separate compositor thread, so scrolling stays smooth even if the page is doing a lot of work on the main thread. Desktop Firefox (Gecko) uses a similar approach where scrolling can be handled off the main thread, so it isn’t blocked by JavaScript and still feels fluid. Many desktop Chromium-based browsers keep scrolling tied to the main thread for heavier web apps, so when React/layout work or other CPU-heavy tasks run, you feel stutters. Large DOM trees, live updates, crypto/identity logic, or frequent async updates are exactly the kinds of things that make the browser’s scroll architecture noticeable.

title: Will the native app UI changes be applied to the web/desktop version, and are there plans to add more uses for the OpenChat (CHAT) token in either version?
text:
Will the native app UI changes be applied to the web/desktop version, and are there plans to add more uses for the OpenChat (CHAT) token in either version?

The new UI will be released on the native app first. The team views that design as the future for mobile web and has built reusable UI components so they can later refactor the desktop/web UI while preserving differences between mobile and desktop. The native changes are being kept separate initially to avoid breaking the existing site and to allow faster, safer development; they expect to gather feedback, fix bugs, then merge and clean up technical debt when ready. Regarding CHAT token uses: yes—there are plans to expand uses of CHAT (for example, monetization of bots is a likely area to add value).

title: How do I update the Open Chat (OC) Android app?
text:
How do I update the Open Chat (OC) Android app?

If you’re on Android it depends on which build you have. To be certain you’re on the latest beta, uninstall the current app and install the newest APK from the project’s releases page (for example, the Open Chat Labs releases on GitHub). The full-release APK should generally update itself by automatically downloading and applying updates.

title: What is a chit?
text:

A chit is like experience points (XP). You can use chits to customize your profile, and if you have enough, you may be eligible to claim prizes that other people offer (if the prize-giver requires a minimum number of chits).

title: I can't change an item back to private — what should I try and what might cause it to fail?
text:
I can't change an item back to private — what should I try and what might cause it to fail?

Open the item’s details and switch the privacy setting back to private. If the change doesn’t take on the first attempt (for example, nothing happens after clicking Update), try again — intermittent internet/connectivity issues can cause the update to fail temporarily.
